# robot-toast — full API reference (AI-optimized)

This file describes the current **v2 API** (published as `robot-toast@beta`).
The default `npm install robot-toast` still resolves to **v1.x** until v2
graduates out of beta. If you are generating code without knowing the user's
installed version, prefer the v2 API and note the installation command.

Zero runtime dependencies. React is an **optional** peer dep, used only if
the consumer imports from `robot-toast/react`.

---

## Install

```bash
# v1.x (current default on npm)
npm install robot-toast

# v2.x (beta)
npm install robot-toast@beta
```

No CSS import is required — styles are auto-injected at runtime (SSR-safe; DOM
access is guarded).

---

## Entry points

```ts
import { toast, RobotToast, /* types */ } from 'robot-toast';
import * as robots from 'robot-toast/robots';            // 16 data-URL exports
import { useRobotToast, useToastOnMount } from 'robot-toast/react';
```

Each subpath has its own bundle; `robot-toast/robots` is tree-shakeable.

---

## Core usage

```ts
import { toast } from 'robot-toast';

// String form — just the message, all other options default
toast('Hello');

// Options form — any fields may be passed
toast({
  message:  'Saved!',
  type:     'success',
  position: 'top-right',
  theme:    'dark',
});

// Return value is a numeric id (useful for closeById)
const id = toast('Working…');
toast.closeById(id);
toast.closeAll();

// Typed shorthands — set `type` automatically
toast.success('Saved');
toast.error('Failed');
toast.info('FYI');
toast.warning('Heads up');

// Promise lifecycle
toast.promise(fetch('/api/save'), {
  loading: 'Saving…',
  success: 'Saved!',                                   // or: (value) => `Saved #${value.id}`
  error:   'Save failed',                              // or: (err)   => `Error: ${err.message}`
});
// The promise's resolution/rejection passes through untouched —
// `await toast.promise(...)` still yields the resolved value or throws.
```

---

## Robot images (v2 — opt-in)

v1 passed robot names as strings (`robotVariant: 'wave'`). v2 removed that
lookup to make the package tree-shakeable. The four possible shapes for
`robotVariant` in v2:

| Value | Effect |
|---|---|
| *omitted* / `undefined` / `''` / `'none'` | **No robot rendered.** This is the default. |
| `'default'` | Built-in inline SVG (no network fetch, no extra import). |
| Any string starting with `data:` | Rendered as `<img>` — used with imports from `robot-toast/robots`. |
| Path ending in `.svg` / `.png` / `.jpg` / `.jpeg` / `.gif` / `.webp` | Rendered as `<img>` from the given path. |
| Any other string | **Hidden.** Legacy v1 names like `'wave'` fall here in v2 and do NOT render. |

Usage with built-in variants:

```ts
import { toast } from 'robot-toast';
import { wave, success, error as errorRobot, headPalm } from 'robot-toast/robots';

toast({ message: 'Hi',       robotVariant: wave });
toast({ message: 'Saved',    robotVariant: success,    type: 'success' });
toast({ message: 'Failed',   robotVariant: errorRobot, type: 'error'   });
toast({ message: 'Confused', robotVariant: headPalm });
```

### All 16 built-in identifiers in `robot-toast/robots`

`wave`, `base`, `base2`, `success`, `error`, `angry`, `angry2`, `shock`,
`think`, `search`, `loading`, `sleep`, `headPalm`, `typing`, `validation`,
`validation2`.

Two renames vs v1:

- v1 `'head-palm'` → v2 `headPalm` (dashes aren't valid JS identifiers)
- v1 `'type'`      → v2 `typing`   (to avoid parse ambiguity with TypeScript's `import { type … }` syntax)

---

## React bindings

```tsx
import { useRobotToast, useToastOnMount } from 'robot-toast/react';

function SaveButton() {
  const toast = useRobotToast();                  // stable reference to `toast`
  return <button onClick={() => toast.success('Saved!')}>Save</button>;
}

function LoadingBanner() {
  // Fires the toast on mount, closes it on unmount.
  // Options are captured ONCE at mount — not updated on re-renders.
  useToastOnMount({ message: 'Fetching…', autoClose: false });
  return null;
}
```

React ≥ 16.8 is required as a peer dependency for this subpath. Non-React
consumers aren't affected.

---

## Full options reference

```ts
interface RobotToastOptions {
  message:           string;                       // required

  // Appearance
  type?:             'default' | 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error';   // default: 'default'
  theme?:            'light' | 'dark' | 'colored';                            // default: 'light'
  transition?:       'bounce' | 'slide' | 'zoom' | 'flip';                    // default: 'bounce'
  position?:         'top-left'    | 'top-center'    | 'top-right'
                   | 'bottom-left' | 'bottom-center' | 'bottom-right';        // default: 'bottom-right'
  style?:            Record<string, string | number>;                         // inline CSS for the message bubble

  // Robot — see the Robot section above
  robotVariant?:     string;                       // default: omitted = no robot
  nearScreen?:       boolean;                      // default: true. Robot on screen-edge side vs inner side

  // Timing
  autoClose?:        number | false;               // default: 5000 (ms). false = stays until dismissed
  typeSpeed?:        number;                       // default: 30 (ms per character). 0 = instant

  // Behaviour
  hideProgressBar?:  boolean;                      // default: false
  draggable?:        boolean;                      // default: true. Releases snap to nearest horizontal edge
  pauseOnHover?:     boolean;                      // default: true
  pauseOnFocusLoss?: boolean;                      // default: true
  rtl?:              boolean;                      // default: false

  // Multi-toast
  limit?:            number;                       // default: 0 (unlimited). Excess is auto-queued
  newestOnTop?:      boolean;                      // default: false

  // Lifecycle callbacks
  onOpen?:           () => void;
  onClose?:          () => void;
}
```

---

## Kitchen-sink example

```ts
import { toast } from 'robot-toast';
import { wave } from 'robot-toast/robots';

toast({
  message:     'Fully configured toast',
  type:        'success',
  theme:       'dark',
  transition:  'bounce',
  position:    'bottom-right',
  robotVariant: wave,
  nearScreen:  true,
  autoClose:   5000,
  typeSpeed:   30,
  hideProgressBar:  false,
  draggable:        true,
  pauseOnHover:     true,
  pauseOnFocusLoss: true,
  rtl:         false,
  limit:       0,
  newestOnTop: false,
  style: {
    background:   'linear-gradient(135deg, #667eea, #764ba2)',
    color:        '#fff',
    borderRadius: '16px',
  },
  onOpen:  () => console.log('shown'),
  onClose: () => console.log('dismissed'),
});
```

---

## v1 → v2 breaking changes (quick checklist)

1. Omitting `robotVariant` now hides the robot. In v1 it showed the default.
   **Fix:** add `robotVariant: 'default'` where you want a robot with no import.
2. String names like `robotVariant: 'wave'` no longer work.
   **Fix:** `import { wave } from 'robot-toast/robots'` and pass `wave`.
3. `'head-palm'` → `headPalm`, `'type'` → `typing`.
4. The `ROBOT_IMAGES` export is removed. Import individual variants instead.
5. Dragging the toast never dismisses; it always snaps to the nearest edge.
   Dismissal only happens via the close button, `closeById()`, `closeAll()`,
   or auto-close expiry.

---

## Accessibility

- `error` / `warning` toasts get `role="alert"` + `aria-live="assertive"`.
- Other types get `role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"`.
- All toasts have `aria-atomic="true"`.
- The close button has `type="button"` + `aria-label="Dismiss notification"`.

---

## Bundle sizes (v2, unminified + ungzipped)

- Core (`robot-toast`): 39 KB
- `robot-toast/robots` barrel with all 16 variants: 23 KB (tree-shakes per named import)
- `robot-toast/react` hook bundle: < 500 B (peer-deps React and re-imports core)

Core is SSR-safe — all `document`/`window` access is guarded, so importing
does not throw during Next.js/Nuxt/Remix server rendering.

---

## Stability

v2.x is currently **beta**. The public API shown above is the one that will
ship as v2.0.0 stable — no further breaking changes are planned before
promotion. v1.x remains the `latest` dist-tag on npm until v2 graduates.
